answer: Make every agent lock a refundable stake before it can trade, slashed on proven fraud. One identity means one bond, so spawning a thousand fake agents costs a thousand bonds, and the attack only pays at the nadir of the stake price — a bad bet. Picture the registry as a lagoon with a single narrow inlet: honest agents pass through cheaply, but flooding it with fakes drains the attacker's capital faster than any profit they can extract.
